text: Mainly because they give people control. You can watch what you want, when you want and on any device, without waiting for a particular time or sitting through adverts. Streaming services also invest heavily in their own series, which attracts huge audiences. Traditional channels still have an advantage for live events like news or football, so I think they'll survive but become smaller.

tips.ru: They'll survive but become smaller — без крайностей.

text: Occasionally it's fine — it's one of the pleasures of a long winter weekend. The problem starts when it becomes a habit. Streaming platforms automatically start the next episode after a few seconds, so it's very easy to stay up until three in the morning without really deciding to. Regular sleep loss affects concentration and mood, so it's worth switching off that autoplay function.

text: Age ratings already exist, but on streaming platforms they're very easy to ignore, because children often use their parents' accounts. I think the technology for separate children's profiles is good enough; the problem is that many parents don't use it. So rather than stricter laws, I'd focus on helping parents understand the settings and talk to their children about what they watch.

text: It's very important, because films and series shape how people see their own country and how others see it too. If everything people watch is foreign, local stories and humour slowly disappear. Kazakh cinema has become much stronger recently, and some comedies have beaten Hollywood films at local cinemas. Support for young directors would help the industry grow even further.

text: For language learners, subtitles are much better, because you hear the real voices and pick up pronunciation without noticing. Subtitles also keep the actors' original performance, which is often lost in dubbing. On the other hand, dubbing is easier for children and older people who read slowly. I'd say the ideal is to offer both, which most streaming services already do.
